toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
What is going on: the departures are concentrated in the Kestrel review team, not spread across the group. Eight of the eleven associates on Kestrel resigned, against one of the thirteen who were never on it. Kestrel associates also logged more hours (about 2,270 against 1,940) and far more weekend work. Every Kestrel associate had the same supervising partner, Dorian Faulk, so the records cannot separate his supervision from the workload. Pay and the firm-wide billable target do not fit the pattern, since they apply to everyone.

How sure: moderate. The link to Kestrel is strong. Whether workload or supervision is the cause is not yet established, and recorded hours may understate late-night work.

What to do next: do not pay the group-wide retention payment or close the review yet, since it would not address the cause and would hide the signal. Commission the confidential interviews, structured to separate supervision from workload, before choosing between moving supervision or adding review capacity. Start adding matter and supervisor fields to attrition reporting now.
output.methodChoice: Collected X7 (matter and supervisor records) and X9 (recorded hours); stopped at two items.
